• Gondi, their mother tongue, is a member of the **Dravidian language** family.
 
• The Gondi community has been featured in two major films: **S.S. Rajamouli's 2022 blockbuster RRR and the 2017 Amit V. Masurkar film Newton**.

• It is a community in **Andhra Pradesh**.

• **Bhils:**
 
 
• These are a large tribal community primarily found in western India, including the states of **Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Madhya Pradesh**. 
 
• A subgroup of the Western Zone of the Indo-Aryan languages, they speak the **Bhil languages**.
 
 
 
• **Chenchus:**
 
 
• These are another tribal community primarily found in **Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and parts of Karnataka**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the objectives of the NITI Aayog?

options.text: To develop mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level
To design and print new currency notes and to bring them in circulation
To pay special attention to the sections of our society that may be at risk of not benefiting adequately from economic progress.
To evolve a shared vision of national development priorities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The design and printing of currency notes and their circulation is not one of the objectives of the **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India).**
 
• **The NITI Aayog** is a policy think tank of the Government of India that primarily focuses on strategic and long-term planning for the country's development.
 
• It acts as a platform for cooperative federalism, fostering the involvement of **states in policy formulation and implementation**.
 
• The responsibility for the design, printing, and circulation of currency notes in India lies with the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, which is the central banking institution of the country.
 
• **The RBI **is responsible for formulating and implementing monetary policy, issuing currency notes, and regulating the overall banking and financial system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The NITI Aayog, or the National Institution for Transforming India,** is a policy think tank of the **Government of India.**
 
• It was established on** January 1, 2015**, to replace the erstwhile Planning Commission.
 
• **The NITI Aayog's primary objective **is to provide strategic and long-term policy inputs to the central and state governments to foster sustainable and inclusive development across various sectors of the Indian economy.
 
• **The key functions and objectives of the NITI Aayog include:**
 
 
• **Formulating strategic and long-term development plans: **The NITI Aayog formulates and recommends strategic plans, medium-term and long-term development frameworks, and policies for various sectors of the economy.
 
• **Cooperative federalism:** The NITI Aayog promotes cooperative federalism by fostering the involvement of state governments in policy formulation and implementation, ensuring their active participation and contribution in the planning process.
 
• **Policy research and innovation: **The NITI Aayog conducts research, analysis, and evidence-based policy studies on various social and economic issues to identify challenges, suggest innovative solutions, and provide policy recommendations to the government.
 
• **Monitoring and evaluation: **The NITI Aayog monitors and evaluates the implementation of policies and programs, assesses their outcomes, and suggests mid-course corrections, if required, to achieve desired development goals.
 
• **International cooperation: **The NITI Aayog facilitates international cooperation and exchange of best practices in policy planning and development with other countries and international organizations.
 
• **Collaborative platforms: **The NITI Aayog provides a platform for collaboration and dialogue among various stakeholders, including government agencies, experts, academicians, industry representatives, and civil society organizations, to foster participative and inclusive policy-making.
 
• It's important to note that the NITI Aayog's role is primarily advisory in nature, and the responsibility for implementing policies and executing projects lies with the respective ministries and departments of the central and state governments.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution prohibits trafficking in human beings and forced labour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer __**Article 23**__.

__
 
• **Article 23 of the Indian Constitution prohibits trafficking in human beings and forced labour.**

 
 
• The Right against Exploitation is enshrined in **Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• These are** important Fundamental Rights** that guarantee every citizen protection from any kind of forced labour.
 
• Everyone has the** right to work, to free choice of employment, to just and favourable conditions of work, and to protection against unemployment.**
 
• Everyone, without any discrimination, has the right to equal pay for equal work.
 
• **Laws passed by the Parliament in pursuance of Article 23:**
 
 
• **Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956**
 
• **Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976**
 
 
 
• Article 23 protects citizens not only against the State but also from private citizens.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The right to equality is guaranteed by **the Constitution in Articles 14 – 18.**
 
• It provides for** the equal treatment of everyone before the law, prevents discrimination on various grounds, treats everybody as equals in matters of public employment, and abolishes untouchability, and titles.**
 
• **Article 23(1):**
 
 
• **​** Traffic in human beings and the beggar and other similar forms of forced labour are prohibited and any contravention of this provision shall be an offence punishable in accordance with the law.
 
 
 
• **Article 23(2):**
 
 
• Nothing in this article shall prevent the State from imposing compulsory service for public purposes, and in imposing such service the State shall not make any discrimination on grounds only of religion, race, caste or class or any of them.

• It was established by Article 169. It is a permanent committee chosen from the meets of both houses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Chief minister and its cabinet__ is the major members of the house of the parliament which as per the Chief minister are considered as the major people of the most importance.
 
• They work for the functioning of the administration and are assigned the work of the different departments.
 
• __Chief minister__ 
 __
 
• Article 164 says that the Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Governor, though the constitution does not contain any specific procedure for the selection and appointment of the Chief Minister.
 
• In accordance with the conventions of the parliamentary system of Government, the Governor appoints the leader of the majority party in the state legislative as Chief Minister.
 
• The chief minister may be a member of any of the two houses of state legislatures.
 
 
 
• Governor of the state__* *is also the vice chancellor of all the government colleges within the state .
 
• Appointed by the president looks for the functioning of peace and law within the state.

questions.question: Out of the given four alternatives, select the one that is NOT a constitutional body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Human Rights Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **India**, a Constitutional body is a body or **institute **established by the **Constitution of India**. They can only be **created **or **changed **by passing a **constitutional amendment bill**, rather than an **Act of Parliament**.
 
• The **National Human Rights Commission **of **India **is a **statutory public body **constituted on **12 October 1993 **under the **Protection of Human Rights Ordinance of 28 September 1993**.
 
• It was **given **a statutory basis by the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993**.
 
• **Arun Kumar Mishra**, a **former Judge of the Supreme Court **is the **current chairperson of the commission **(11th chairperson of NHRC). 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Finance Commissions **are commissions **periodically constituted **by the **President of India **under **Article 280 **of the **Indian Constitution **to define the **financial relations **between the **central government of India **and the **individual state governments**.
 
• The **Election Commission of India **is a **constitutional body**. It was established by the **Constitution of India **to **conduct **and **regulate elections **in the **country**.
 
• The **Union Public Service Commission**, commonly abbreviated as **UPSC**, is **India's premier central recruitment agency **for recruitment of all the **Group 'A' officers **under the **Government of India**.

questions.question: In which year did NITI Aayog come into existence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __2015__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Planning Commission was replaced by a new institution – NITI AAYYOG on January 1, 2015,** with emphasis on **‘Bottom –Up’ approach **to envisage the vision of Maximum Governance, Minimum Government, echoing the spirit of **‘Cooperative Federalism**’.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative Skeltal**

 
 
• **Chairperson: Prime Minister**
 
• Vice-Chairperson: To be appointed by Prime-Minister
 
• **Governing Council:** Chief Ministers of all states and Lt. Governors of Union Territories.
 
• Regional Council: To address specific regional issues, Comprising Chief Ministers and Lt. Governors Chaired by Prime Minister or his nominee.
 
• Adhoc Membership: 2 members in ex-officio capacity from leading Research institutions on a rotational basis.
 
• **Ex-Officio membership: Maximum four from Union council of ministers to be nominated by Prime minister.**
 
• Chief Executive Officer: Appointed by Prime-minister for a fixed tenure, in the rank of Secretary to Government of India.
 
• Special Invitees: Experts, Specialists with domain knowledge nominated by Prime-minister.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog Hubs**
 
 
• Team India Hub acts as an interface between States and Centre.
 
• Knowledge and Innovation Hub builds the think-tank acumen of NITI Aayog.
